(a) Review of Payment of Compensation.—Section 415(e) of the Plant Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 7715(e)) is amended in the second sentence by striking “of longer than 60 days”. 
    (b) Secretarial Discretion.—Section 442(c) of the Plant Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 7772(c)) is amended by striking “of longer than 60 days”. 
    (c) Subpoena Authority.—Section 423 of the Plant Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 7733) is amended—
        (1) by striking subsection (a) and inserting the following:“(a) Authority to Issue.—The Secretary shall have the power to subpoena the attendance and testimony of any witness, the production of all evidence (including books, papers, documents, electronically stored information, and other tangible things that constitute or contain evidence), or to require the person to whom the subpoena is directed to permit the inspection of premises relating to the administration or enforcement of this title or any matter under investigation in connection with this title.”; 
        (2) in subsection (b), by striking “documentary”; and 
        (3) in subsection (c)—
            (A) in the first sentence, by striking “testimony of any witness and the production of documentary evidence” and inserting “testimony of any witness, the production of evidence, or the inspection of premises”; and 
            (B) in the second sentence, by striking “question or to produce documentary evidence” and inserting “question, produce evidence, or permit the inspection of premises”.   
    (d) Willful Violations.—Section 424(b)(1)(A) of the Plant Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 7734(b)(1)(A)) is amended by striking “and $500,000 for all violations adjudicated in a single proceeding” and inserting “$500,000 for all violations adjudicated in a single proceeding if the violations do not include a willful violation, and $1,000,000 for all violations adjudicated in a single proceeding if the violations include a willful violation”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that subpoenaed witness testimony or the heading "Review of Payment of Compensation" involves outside parties in a federal decision. But a subpoena is compelled evidence-gathering for enforcement and investigation, not consultation, and the review amendments only strike a time qualifier without granting anyone a right to sue or object. The rest of the section just raises civil penalty caps, so nothing here creates a comment period, hearing, advisory body, or outside consultation.
fable.s: The Secretary shall have the power to subpoena the attendance and testimony of any witness

opus.w: This section expands the Secretary's subpoena power, removes a 60-day qualifier in two provisions, and raises civil penalty caps for willful violations. A subpoena forces witnesses to provide evidence in an enforcement setting. It is not a chance for outside parties to advise on or help shape a federal decision. Nothing here creates a comment period, public hearing, advisory committee, consultation with states or tribes, or a right to sue.
opus.s: The Secretary shall have the power to subpoena the attendance and testimony of any witness, the production of all evidence
opus.b: The answer is **No**. The tempting reading is that the subpoena power to compel "the attendance and testimony of any witness" counts as participation, since it brings outsiders into contact with the government. It doesn't fit the definition. A subpoena is an investigative and enforcement tool: the Secretary forces people to provide evidence. It is not consultation with outsiders before a policy decision. The other subsections only change deadline wording ("of longer than 60 days") and civil penalty caps. None of them adds a comment period, hearing, advisory body, state or tribal consultation, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Plant Protection Act to clarify subpoena authority, payment review timelines, and penalty amounts. Subpoena power is an enforcement mechanism to compel evidence from outside parties, not a form of consultation or coordination where outside parties advise the government before a decision is made. The other amendments concern internal administrative procedures or penalty structures, which do not involve outside participation.
qwen_chat.s: (c) Subpoena Authority.—Section 423 of the Plant Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 7733) is amended— (1) by striking subsection (a) and inserting the following:“(a) Authority to Issue.—The Secretary shall have the power to subpoena the attendance and testimony of any witness, the production of all evidence... or to require the person to whom the subpoena is directed to permit the inspection of premises relating to the administration or enforcement of this title or any matter under investigation in connection with this title.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the subpoena authority allows the government to compel participation from outside parties (witnesses, producers of evidence). However, the definition of participation requires that the government *consult or coordinate* with outside parties *before* making a decision, or that outside parties have a right to sue/object. Subpoenas are enforcement tools used to gather facts for an investigation or proceeding, not a mechanism for collaborative decision-making or advisory input. The outside party is compelled to provide evidence, not invited to advise or consult. Furthermore, the other amendments relate to internal agency procedures (payment review, secretarial discretion) or penalty amounts, none of which involve outside participation.
